t:
That 

    (a) 
the Tariff Schedules of the United States (19 U.S.C. 1202) are amended as follows:

        (1) 
Item 417.12 (relating to aluminum hydroxide and oxide (alumina)) is amended by striking out “0.15¢ per lb.” and inserting in lieu thereof “Free”.
 
        (2) 
Item 521.17 (relating to bauxite, calcined) is amended by striking out “11¢ per ton” and inserting in lieu thereof “Free”.
 
        (3) 
Item 601.06 (relating to bauxite ore) is amended by striking out “100per ton” and inserting in lieu thereof “Free”.
 
        (4) 
Effective July 16, 1971, items 907.15 (relating to aluminum oxide (alumina) when imported for use in producing aluminum), 909.30 (relating to bauxite, calcined), and 911.05 (relating to bauxite ore) are repealed.
  
    (b) 
The rates of duty for items 417.12, 521.17, and 601.06 in rate column numbered 1 of the Tariff Schedules of the United States, as amended by subsection (a), shall (1) be treated as not having the status of statutory provision enacted by the Congress, but as having been proclaimed by the President as being required or appropriate to carrying out foreign trade agreements to which the United States is a party, and (2) supersede the staged rates of duty provided for such items in Annex III to Proclamation 3822, dated December 16, 1967 (32 Fed. Reg., No. 244, part II, p. 19037).
 
    (c) 
The amendments made by subsection (a) shall apply with respect to articles entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for consumption after July 15, 1971.

fable.w: This section directly amends tariff schedules to make alumina and bauxite duty-free and sets effective dates. The tempting reading is that the reference to "foreign trade agreements" or a presidential proclamation implies consultation with outside parties, but that language only assigns a legal status to the rates. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, consultation, or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government.
fable.s: be treated as not having the status of statutory provision enacted by the Congress, but as having been proclaimed by the President as being required or appropriate to carrying out foreign trade agreements to which the United States is a party

qwen_block.w: This section amends tariff schedules to change duty rates on specific goods. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities) in the decision-making process. The changes are legislative amendments to statutory rates, not a procedural requirement for outside input.
qwen_block.s: Item 417.12 (relating to aluminum hydroxide and oxide (alumina)) is amended by striking out “0.15¢ per lb.” and inserting in lieu thereof “Free”.

opus.w: This section changes certain tariff rates to free, repeals some items and sets effective dates. No outside party is consulted or involved in any federal decision. The mention of 'foreign trade agreements' only describes the legal status of the rates by reference to agreements that already exist. Like the past agreement in Example 5, it is not a future process that brings outsiders into a decision.
opus.s: shall (1) be treated as not having the status of statutory provision enacted by the Congress, but as having been proclaimed by the President as being required or appropriate to carrying out foreign trade agreements to which the United States is a party
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The phrase "foreign trade agreements to which the United States is a party" could look like coordination with parties outside the federal government. That reading fails. The phrase only sets the legal status of the new duty rates by treating them as if the President had proclaimed them. It refers to agreements that already exist. It creates no future consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue before a federal decision. Everything else in the section is tariff rate changes and effective dates.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends tariff schedules by changing duty rates to 'Free' or repealing items. It does not require consultation, public comment, or coordination with any outside parties (such as states, tribes, or the public) before these changes are made. The text describes the legislative action itself, not a participatory process.
qwen_chat.s: Item 417.12 (relating to aluminum hydroxide and oxide (alumina)) is amended by striking out “0.15¢ per lb.” and inserting in lieu thereof “Free”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing tariff rates affects the public or companies, so it involves participation. However, the text itself only describes legislative amendments to tariff schedules and their legal status. It does not mandate any process for consulting with the public, states, or other outside entities before making these changes. The changes are enacted directly by Congress (or attributed to Presidential proclamation based on prior agreements), without a required participatory mechanism in this specific section.
